headline: Approved zoning variances for a new house at 11 Billington Avenue and a deck at 42 Browning Street; continued Lavender Waves Farm appeal.
summary: The board heard an appeal of a notice of violation at 3812 Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry Highway over advertising for non-farm events at Lavender Waves Farm. The applicant's attorney said no weddings have been booked that he knows of. Members want the farm's website advertising checked and taken down.
decisions: Continued the appeal of the notice of violation to September 16, 2026, 5-0.
Approved a dimensional variance to replace a 982 sq. ft. deck at 42 Browning Street, 5-0.
Approved a dimensional variance to demolish two dwellings and build a new house at 11 Billington Avenue, 5-0.

decision_titles: Violation appeal at 3812 Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry Highway
plain_text:
Town of South Kingstown   
Zoning Board of Review Meeting   
Meeting Minutes 
Wednesday, August 19, 2026 at 7:00 PM   
South Kingstown Town Hall, Town Council Chambers 
180 High Street, Wakefield, RI 02879 
www.southkingstownri.gov  
Robert Cagnetta, Chair 
Thomas Daniels, Vice Chair 
Geoff Elia, Member 
Arlene Hicks, Member 
William MacDonald, Member 
Vacancy, Alt. #1 
Vacancy, Alt. #2 
 
A. Call to Order 
Mr. Cagnetta called the meeting to order at 7:00:43 PM. 
B. Chairman Introductions and Instructions 
Mr. Cagnetta explained the rules and procedures.   
 
William MacDonald was promoted from Alternate #1 to Board Member by the Town Council on August 11, 2026. 
 
Members Present: Robert Cagnetta, Chairman; Thomas Daniels, Vice Chairman; Arlene Hicks, Member; Geoff 
Elia, Member; William MacDonald, Member. 
 
Members Absent: None 
 
Staff Present: David Marks, Town Legal Counsel; Jamie Gorman, Building and Zoning Official; Ben Barbera, 
Building and Zoning Associate. 
 
Members voting tonight will be Mr. Cagnetta, Mr. Daniels, Ms. Hicks, Mr. Elia and Mr. MacDonald. 
C. Agenda Items *Order can be subject to change* 
Mr. Cagnetta called for the first petition. 
 I. Continuation of petition ZA-26-1: Henry Cabrera, 3812 Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry Highway, 
Wakefield, RI 02879, for an Appeal under the Zoning Ordinance as follows: The applicant is seeking 
to Appeal a Notice of Violation issued by the Zoning Enforcement Officer (ZEO), dated May 22, 
2025, related to premises at 3812 Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry Highway. The owner of the property 
is Henry Cabrera, for premises located at 3812 Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry Highway, South 
Kingstown, Assessor’s Map 78-3, Lot 7 and is zoned R200. 
3812 Comm O H Hwy - Application 
All the material was recognized and entered into the record.  
 
This petition is continued from the May 20, 2026, Zoning Board of Review Meeting. 
 
Attorney Stephen Angell, representing the applicant, was present and duly sworn in. 
 
The applicant is currently working with the town's planning department to create a development plan review. The 
applicant is also in talks with CRMC since the town would like the applicant to get a permit of use from CRMC. The 
applicant also stated that it took some time to find a landscape architect to come up with a landscape plan. Mr. 
Angell will hopefully have the landscaping plan ready next week. Lastly, they have been developing a traffic 
memorandum just short of a full traffic stop. 
 
Mr. Angell goes on to say that he does not expect to hear anything from CRMC within the next couple of months. 
Mr. Angell then requested a continuation of the petition to the November or December 2026, Zoning Board of 
Review meeting. 
 
Mr. Cagnetta reminds Mr. Angell that the Zoning Officer required Lavender Waves Farm to cease any advertising for 
events that are not farm related.
Mr. Angell acknowledges by stating that his client does not intend to have weddings of the scale that he was 
seeking to have. 
 
Board questions ensued. 
 
Mr. Elia asks if Lavender Waves Farms is planning to have any events that are not farm related. 
 
Mr. Angell answers that there will not be any events that are not farm-related. 
 
Mr. Cagnetta asks Jamie Gorman, Zoning Officer, if this satisfies his concerns in relation to the notice of violation. 
 
Mr. Gorman answers that the initial notice of violation was about advertising weddings and other events that were 
non-agricultural. 
 
Mr. Cagnetta asks where the complaints came from. 
 
Mr. Gorman states that it was brought to his attention by neighbors who have issues with traffic, noise, music, and 
things of that nature. Mr. Gorman goes on to say that farm-related events are permitted, such as lavender picking 
and events including animals. 
 
Mr. Angell has instructed his client not to have any events at Lavender Waves Farm which are not agricultural 
related. 
 
Mr. Daniels comments that the applicant is moving in a positive direction, but this violation is from 2025, and needs 
to be addressed now rather than considering what will happen in the future. 
 
Attorney David Marks, the town's legal counsel, recommends that the board allow the applicant time to reach 
compliance with the town. He advises that the board allows for the requested continuance to see if the town's 
planning board can work something out. 
 
Ms. Hicks asked Mr. Angell if all advertising related to non-farm events had stopped. 
 
Mr. Angell was unsure if the advertising had stopped at the present time. 
 
Mr. MacDonald would like Mr. Angell to confirm with his client that there is no advertising currently and to let the 
building official know in a timely manner. 
 
At this time, Jamie Gorman presented a current view of Lavender Waves Farm's website. There is a link labeled 
"Weddings/Events." Although the text does not say wedding, it does include other events like birthdays, 
anniversaries, showers, and reunions. 
 
Ms. Hicks adds that until this violation is resolved, Lavender Waves Farm should stop advertising. 
 
Mr. Gorman summarizes that Lavender Waves Farm is not permitted, as of right, to conduct non-farming-related 
events. He explained that the planning board may authorize such events through a Development Plan Review, 
which would establish specific conditions and parameters governing the events that must be adhered to. 
 
Mr. Cagnetta explains that Lavender Waves Farm was explicitly told that they should not be advertising a year and a 
half ago, yet they still are. He asked Mr. Angell if he can confirm that no events have been booked for calendar year 
2027. 
 
Mr. Angell replies that no weddings have been booked, which he is aware of.  
 
Mr. Daniels contributes that, based on what he has seen, Lavender Waves Farm is still in violation. 
 
Mr. Cagnetta recommends to the other board members that this petition be continued to the September 16, 2026, 
zoning board meeting. He would like the board to verify that the advertising on the website has been taken down.
Attorney Marks comments that the board cannot add a condition to a continuation, but they can certainly request 
that the advertising be removed in order to grant a further continuance. 
 
There were no further board questions. 
 
Whereas the following motion was made. 
 
The motion is as follows:  
The following motion to continue the petition to the September 16, 2026, Zoning Board Meeting was made 
by Mr. Elia and duly seconded by Mr. Cagnetta. 
Motion passed unanimously: (5-0 Vote in favor)    
(Mr. Elia -Aye, Mr. Cagnetta -Aye, Mr. Daniels -Aye, Ms. Hicks -Aye, Mr. MacDonald -Aye)                                   
                                                                        
________________________________ 
 
Mr. Cagnetta called for the next petition. 
 II. Continuation of petition ZBR-26-21: Andrew Shea, 231 Briarwood Drive, Wakefield, RI 02879, 
requests a Dimensional Variance under the Zoning Ordinance as follows: The applicant is seeking to 
replace a 982 sq. ft. deck at the rear of the dwelling. The deck will be located 1'2" from the east side 
property line and 4'2" from the north side property line. The required side yard setback is 4'6", therefore, 
relief of 3'4" and 4" is requested. Lot size is .21 acre. A Dimensional Variance is required per Zoning 
Ordinance Section 205 (Single Nonconforming Lots) and Section 907 (Standards of Relief). 
Owners of the property are Gary & Constance Wyllie for premises located at 42 Browning Street, South 
Kingstown, Assessor’s Map 96-1, Lot 47 and is zoned R30. 
42 Browning Street - Application 
All the material was recognized and entered into the record. 
 
This petition is continued from the July 15, 2026, Zoning Board meeting. 
 
Andrew Shea, general contractor, and Constance Wyllie, property owner, were present and duly sworn in. 
 
Ms. Wyllie handed out "Applicants Exhibit 1" to the board members. Exhibit 1 included property records and aerial 
photos throughout the years. 
 
Ms. Wyllie states that she and her husband bought the property in October 2022. Prior to that, the Wyllie's rented 
the house for 30 years. Ms. Wyllie begins by going over her exhibit 1 packet that she handed out earlier. 
 
Mr. Cagnetta redirected the discussion to the proposed deck for which Ms. Wyllie is seeking approval. 
 
Ms. Wyllie explains that she is replacing the deck in kind. The proposed deck will have the same footings and 
decking area as the original. Ms. Wyllie added that the packet she provided includes photographs documenting the 
deck over the past ten years. Mr. Shea did apply for a building permit before the work commenced, but he was 
unaware of prior setbacks that were required. Ms. Wyllie would like to replace the deck in order to modernize the 
home. She also felt that the deck was in disrepair and potentially dangerous when her grandchildren came to visit. 
 
Mr. Gorman, Building Official, states that Mr. Shea was working under a building permit. The building department 
was made aware that there may be an encroachment issue. Building inspectors went out where they saw that the 
deck framing was already complete. Typically, the building department does not require a survey for a deck 
replacement, but upon inspection there were survey markers and clear lines that were measured. The building 
inspector was unable to tell if the deck that they were replacing was damaged or if they were able to replace it in 
kind without a variance. Mr. Gorman states that the new deck appears to be the same size as the original. 
 
Mr. Cagnetta asks Ms. Wyllie if the measurements that were taken for the new deck are accurate regarding the 
distance from the property line. 
 
Ms. Wyllie states that they are.
Mr. Cagnetta asks Ms. Wyllie how far along the project currently is. 
 
Ms. Wyllie answers that the framing is done, and the decking was put on to make the deck safe. 
 
There were no further board questions for the applicants. 
 
Mr. Cagnetta asked if there was anyone in the audience who wished to speak in favor of the petition. 
 
There was no one present who spoke in favor. 
 
Mr. Cagnetta asked if there was anyone in the audience who wished to speak in opposition to the petition. 
 
Bert Hess, neighbor, was present and duly sworn in. 
 
Mr. Hess passes out his "Objectors Exhibit 1", which is a photograph of what looks like a small expansion to the 
original deck located at 42 Browning Street. 
 
Mr. Hess has lived in his home for 25 years. He states that 25 years ago the deck was roughly 600 square feet. 
Today he believes the deck is over 900 square feet. The portion of the deck he is objecting to is at the back of the 
house as you exit the apartment. Mr. Hess claims that the deck will be three feet from his property line rather than 
4.6 feet.  
 
Mr. Gorman explains that the required setback from the north property line, which abuts Mr. Hess, is 4.6 feet. 
Therefore, there is only 4 inches of encroachment.  
 
Mr. Cagnetta notes that South Kingstown is an old town with many non-conforming lots. Also, Ms. Wyllie's exhibit 1 
proves the deck has not changed over the years. 
 
Ms. Hicks indicates that by viewing the aerial maps she can not see where the deck abuts Mr. Hess's property. 
 
Mr. Hess explains that you can not see the deck because there is a row of trees blocking it from view. 
 
Mr. Elia walked Mr. Hess's property line and stated that he could not see the deck from his property. The existing 
structure and hedge row completely eliminate any view of the deck. 
 
There were no further board questions for Mr. Hess. 
 
Board discussion ensued. 
 
The applicants returned to the podium. 
 
Mr. Cagnetta asks Mr. Shea again if the footprint of the deck has changed. 
 
Mr. Shea is confident that the new deck has the same footprint as the original deck. 
 
There were no further board questions. 
 
Whereas the following motion was made.   
 
The motion is as follows: 
The following motion was made by Mr. Elia and duly seconded by Ms. Hicks. 
Motion approved unanimously: (5-0 Vote in favor)  
(Mr. Elia -Aye, Ms. Hicks -Aye, Mr. MacDonald -Aye, Mr. Daniels -Aye, Mr. Cagnetta -Aye)                                   
                                                                          
 
At a meeting held on August 19, 2026, a motion was made to approve the petition regarding Andrew Shea, 231 
Briarwood Drive, Wakefield, RI 02879, requests a Dimensional Variance under the Zoning Ordinance as follows: 
The applicant is seeking to replace a 982 sq. ft. deck at the rear of the dwelling. The deck will be located 1'2" from 
the east side property line and 4'2" from the north side property line. The required side yard setback is 4'6",
therefore, relief of 3'4" and 4" is requested. Lot size is .21 acre. A Dimensional Variance is required per Zoning 
Ordinance Section 205 (Single Nonconforming Lots) and Section 907 (Standards of Relief). Owners of the 
property are Gary & Constance Wyllie for premises located at 42 Browning Street, South Kingstown, Assessor's 
Map 96-1, Lot 47 and is zoned R30. 
 
The following individual spoke as a representative of the applicant: 
• Constance Wyllie, homeowner. 
• Andrew Shea, general contractor.  
 
There was no one in the audience who wished to speak in favor of the petition. 
 
The following individual was present and spoke in opposition to the permit: 
• Bert Hess, an abutter. 
 
The following materials were entered into the record: 
• Hand Drawn Site Plan with Property Lines, uploaded digitally by Andrew Shea on June 15, 2026 (2 pages). 
Abutters Correspondence #1 dated August 6, 2026, and written by Bertil F. Hess; Building Permit #93295–
42 Browning Street Deck Replacement - the applicant is Andrew Shea and the permit was originally 
approved on May 13, 2026; "Applicant's Exhibit 1" included aria photos and records on the property in 
question, Given to board members during the August 19 meeting. "Objector's Exhibit 1", handed out by Bert 
Hess during the August 19 meeting.  
• 200’ Abutter’s List and Radius Map; Legal Notices; and Notarized Affidavit of Mailing.   
 
Finding of Fact: 
 
1. The Board finds that the hardship from which the applicant seeks relief is due to the unique characteristics of the 
subject land or structure and not to the general characteristics of the surrounding area; and is not due to a physical 
or economic disability of the applicant, excepting those physical disabilities addressed in § 45-24-30(16), because 
the applicant is seeking to replace an existing 982 square foot deck with the exact same footprint and square 
footage at the rear of the dwelling. 
  
2. The Board finds that the hardship is not the result of any prior action of the applicant, because the applicant 
obtained a building permit before they started construction, but they were unaware of the existing setbacks. 
  
3. The Board finds that the granting of the requested variance will not alter the general character of the surrounding 
area or impair the intent or purpose of the zoning ordinance or the comprehensive plan upon which the ordinance is 
based, because the applicant is replacing the existing deck in kind.  
  
4.  The Board finds that the hardship suffered by the owner of the subject property if the dimensional variance is not 
granted amounts to more than a mere inconvenience, meaning that relief sought is minimal to a reasonable 
enjoyment of the permitted use to which the property is proposed to be devoted, because the deck already existed 
and will be replaced in kind. 
  
Approval is conditional subject to the following conditions: 
•  There are no conditions upon this approval. 
 _____________________________________ 
 
Mr. Cagnetta called for the last petition. 
 III. Petition ZBR-26-27: Christopher Santilli, 11 Billington Avenue, South Kingstown, RI 02879. The 
applicant is seeking to demolish two (2) dwellings and construct a new 3-bedroom single-family
dwelling. The new dwelling will be located 8.6' from the front property line. The required front yard 
setback is 11.7', therefore, relief of 3.1' is requested. Lot size is .26 acre. A Dimensional Variance is 
required per Zoning Ordinance Section 205 (Single Nonconforming Lots) and Section 907 
(Standards of Relief). Owner of the property is Eleven Billington, LLC, for premises located at 11 
Billington Avenue, South Kingstown, Assessor’s Map 69-2, Lot 21 and is zoned R40.  
11 Billington Ave. - Application 
All the material was recognized and entered into the record.  
 
Attorney Josh Parks, the applicants' legal counsel, was present and duly sworn in. 
 
The applicant is seeking relief from the front property line setback. The property is a non-conforming lot which has 
an irregular shape. The lot itself is 11,700 square feet in an R40 zone. The relief required from the front setback is 
11.7 feet and the applicant is asking for 8.6 feet. Three feet of relief only pertains to the very north-east corner of the 
property. The lot is in CRMC's jurisdiction because it is within 200 feet of coastal features. The applicants have 
already met with CRMC for a preliminary determination. 
 
Christopher Santilli, property owner, was present and duly sworn in. 
 
Mr. Santilli elaborates that he is seeking to build a three-story house that is within the flood zone. Because of the 
flood zone, the first level of the house will be deemed a non-living space. Living space in a flood zone starts at 13 
feet. During the pre-application meeting with CRMC, biologists required that the proposed house be moved as far as 
possible to the west in order to distance themselves from the marshland. Mr. Santilli is only going for 25% lot 
coverage as opposed to the 50% lot coverage which CRMC allows. The applicant is requesting the relief to preserve 
the intended architectural character of the home. The septic system already exists on the property. Lastly, Mr. 
Santilli states that he submitted a plan to DEM requesting to increase the bedroom count to three bedrooms. 
Currently, the septic system is set up for two bedrooms. 
 
Board questions ensued. 
 
Ms. Hicks asks if DEM does not approve the increase to three bedrooms, will the footprint of the house be altered? 
 
Mr. Santilli answers that the footprint will not be changed. The room that would have been the third bedroom will be 
used for another purpose. 
 
There were no further board questions for the applicant. 
 
Mr. Cagnetta asked if anyone in the audience wished to speak either in favor of or in opposition to the petition.  
 
There was no one in the audience who wished to speak. 
 
There were no further board discussions. 
 
Whereas the following motion was made. 
 
The motion is as follows: 
The following motion was made by Mr. Daniels and duly seconded by Mr. Elia. 
Motion passed unanimously: (5-0 Vote in favor) 
(Mr. Daniels -Aye, Mr. Elia -Aye, Ms. Hicks -Aye, Mr. MacDonald -Aye, Mr. Cagnetta -Aye) 
  
At a meeting held on August 19, 2026, there was a motion to approve the petition regarding Christopher Santilli, 
11 Billington Avenue, South Kingstown, RI 02879. The applicant is seeking to demolish two (2) dwellings and 
construct a new 3-bedroom single-family dwelling. The new dwelling will be located 8.6' from the front property line. 
The required front yard setback is 11.7', therefore, relief of 3.1' is requested. Lot size is .26 acre. A Dimensional 
Variance is required per Zoning Ordinance Section 205 (Single Nonconforming Lots) and Section 907 
(Standards of Relief). Owner of the property is Eleven Billington, LLC, for premises located at 11 Billington Avenue, 
South Kingstown, Assessor’s Map 69-2, Lot 21 and is zoned R40.  
 
The following individuals spoke as representatives of the applicant:
• Attorney Josh Parks, the applicant's legal counsel. 
• Christopher Santilli, applicant. 
 
There was no one from the audience who spoke either in favor of or in opposition to the petition. 
 
The following materials were entered into the record:  
• Survey and Location Plan, produced by E. Greenwich Surveyors, LLC., drawn by Kirk D. Andrews PLS. and 
dated June 1, 2026; Zoning Application Plan — For Proposed Dwelling, produced by E. Greenwich 
Surveyors, LLC., drawn by Kirk D. Andrews PLS. and dated July 9, 2026; Schematic Design, dated August 
11, 2026, uploaded digitally by Chris Santilli (10 pages); RICRMC — Report of Findings, valid after August 
6, 2026, signed by T. Silvia of RICRMC (3 pages); RIDEM Proposed Septic Alteration, dated July 30, 2026, 
designed by Timothy J. Behan P.E. 
• 200’ Abutter’s List and Radius Map; Legal Notices; and Notarized Affidavit of Mailing  
  
Findings of Fact: 
  
1. The Board finds that the hardship from which the applicant seeks relief is due to the unique characteristics of the 
subject land or structure and not to the general characteristics of the surrounding area; and is not due to a physical 
or economic disability of the applicant, excepting those physical disabilities addressed in § 45-24-30(16), because 
the lot has a unique shape and the applicant has done everything they can to ensure construction is away from 
coastal features. The applicant has also taken the necessary steps by obtaining a Preliminary Determination from 
CRMC. 
 
2. The Board finds that the hardship is not the result of any prior action of the applicant, because the applicant has 
taken all the necessary steps prior to gaining approval from the Zoning Board of Review.   
  
3. The Board finds that the granting of the requested variance will not alter the general character of the surrounding 
area or impair the intent or purpose of the zoning ordinance or the comprehensive plan upon which the ordinance is 
based, because this is a neighborhood that has undergone many modernizations over the past several years. This 
petition will be beneficial to the area and neighboring property values. 
  
4.  The Board finds that the hardship suffered by the owner of the subject property if the dimensional variance is not 
granted amounts to more than a mere inconvenience, meaning that relief sought is minimal to a reasonable 
enjoyment of the permitted use to which the property is proposed to be devoted, because the applicant is requesting 
only 3.1 feet of relief from the required front-yard setback, the Board finds that the requested relief is minimal, 
particularly in consideration of the applicant’s efforts to remain respectful of and minimize impacts to the surrounding 
coastal features. 
  
Approval is conditional subject to the following conditions:  
• The decision is conditioned upon any, if necessary, CRMC or RIDEM approvals and will have a two-year 
expiration from the recorded date per Section 908 of the Zoning Ordinance with the right to extend if 
necessary.  
_______________________________________ 
D. Other Items 
 I. Attendance for the September 16, 2026, Zoning Board of Review Meeting 
William MacDonald, Board Member, will not be attending the September 16, 2026, Zoning Board of Review 
Meeting. 
 
All of tonight's other Zoning Board Members will be attending the September 16, 2026, meeting.
II. Approval of the July 15, 2026, Zoning Board of Review Minutes 
There was a motion to approve the Zoning Board of Review Meeting Minutes from July 15, 2026. 
 
The motion is as follows: 
A motion to approve the July 15, 2026, meeting minutes was made by Mr. Cagnetta and seconded by Ms. 
Hicks. 
Motion passed unanimously: (5-0 Vote in favor)   
(Mr. Cagnetta -Aye, Ms. Hicks -Aye, Mr. Daniels -Aye, Mr. MacDonald -Aye, Mr. Elia -Aye) 
 
The July 15, 2026, Meeting Minutes will be published to the public. 
 III. Adjournment  
Mr. Cagnetta made a motion to adjourn the meeting. 
 
All members were in favor. 
 
Meeting adjourned at 8:16:01 PM
